chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
The testimony of women is not valid regarding the new moon.

key_terms.النساء: Women — the plural of imra'a; here used in the context of legal capacity to testify
key_terms.الهلال: The hilal (new crescent moon) — the first visible sliver of the lunar crescent marking the start of a new Islamic month
key_terms.شهادة: Legal testimony (shahadah in juridical sense) — formal witnessing that establishes a fact in law

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women accepted for sighting the new moon (hilal) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) via Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the most authoritative jurists among the companions. The ruling states that the testimony of women alone is insufficient to establish the sighting of the new moon (hilal), which determines the beginning of lunar months including Ramadan, Eid, and Dhul-Hijja. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, the sighting of the crescent moon was a matter of communal religious significance, and Shia fiqh generally requires the testimony of two just men (or other qualifying conditions) to legally establish the new month.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The testimony of the women is not allowed regarding the new moon’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from fro al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Testimony by women is not admissible in the case of seeing the crescent.’”
